pr_title: Handle homekit accessories where the pairing flag is wrong
pr_body:
## Proposed change

Some Homekit devices lie and say they are unpaired when they aren't. The existing code will automatically remove a config entry for such a device (what good is the config entry if the device isn't paired to anything?). But the pairing was actually working, the zeroconf metadata is just incorrect.

So we no longer trust the zeroconf metadata alone and now double check that our pairing keys are actually invalid.

```

                 's#': '1',  # must be 1
                 'sf': '1'  # status flag, lowest bit encodes pairing status, 1 means unpaired
                 }

-            desc['sf'] = '0'
```

issue_context.title: zeroconf integration deletes Animus Heart HomeKit Controller integration upon discovery/restart
issue_context.body:
### The problem

The integration is correctly detected and configured. However, upon restart of core, zeroconf deletes the configuration of the integration and reports it as a newly detected integration, requiring reconfiguration.

Removing "default_config", and replacing it manual variant, except zeroconf:, fixes the issue. 

### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2021.6.3

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

unknown

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

zeroconf

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/zeroconf/

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
# Configure a default setup of Home Assistant (frontend, api, etc)
#default_config:

# Individual options represented by default_config
cloud:
config:
dhcp:
frontend:
history:
input_boolean:
input_datetime:
input_number:
input_select:
input_text:
logbook:
map:
mobile_app:
person:
ssdp:
sun:
system_health:
tag:
timer:
updater:
#zeroconf:
zone:
```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

json deleted from /config/.storage/config_entries upon Animus heart "re-discovery".

`
            {
                "entry_id": "nnn-nnn",
                "version": 1,
                "domain": "homekit_controller",
                "title": "Animus Heart",
                "data": {
                    "AccessoryPairingID": "nnn-nnn",
                    "AccessoryLTPK": "nnn-nnn",
                    "iOSPairingId": "nnn-nnn",
                    "iOSDeviceLTSK": "nnn-nnn",
                    "iOSDeviceLTPK": "nnn-nnn",
                    "AccessoryIP": "192.168.50.31",
                    "AccessoryPort": 9123,
                    "Connection": "IP"
                },
                "options": {},
                "pref_disable_new_entities": false,
                "pref_disable_polling": false,
                "source": "zeroconf",
                "unique_id": "nnn-nnn",
                "disabled_by": null
            }`
comments:
Hey there @jc2k, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with an integration (`homekit_controller`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L214) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

I have seen this before with an uncertified Russian device. It *always* announces itself as unpaired. Home assistant is cleaning up the pairing because the device is claiming there is no pairing. Disabling zeroconf means we don't learn about the devices lies, so we don't unpair it.

I assume the same is happening here, and a bug in the device means that the device is effectively telling home assistant to delete the pairing.

Have you tried this device with iOS? Did it say it was uncertified when you added it?
